It is possible to obtain the sequence of lines in a call (getLineNumberTrace), the values that a variable took within a call (getVariableTrace) or at a particular time stamp (getVariableValue), and the return valuie of the call (getReturnValue). Tools are also available to see the history of a particular primitive value over the whole execution (getVariableHistory). Some analysis of the execution has been done and is made available as well. The set of possible lines that affect the symptom and hence may be buggy can be obtained either for those lines that are executed in the above execution (getFaultLocations) or throughout the whole program (getAllFaultLocations). Most of thsee are not suspicious, but any line that should be changed should be in this set. The history of a particular variable or primitive value, i.e. how and where and when it was changed during the execution, is also available (getVariableHistory). The calls to a particular method, identified by name, is also available (getMethodCalls).
In this case the program has stopped at line $(LINE) in the method $(METHOD). The identified symptom is: $(SYMPTOM). There are no other faults that you neede to consider.
